title: The Mutilated Chessboard
statement: Two diagonally opposite corner squares are removed from an $8\times8$ chessboard. In how many ways can the remaining $62$ squares be tiled by $31$ dominoes?
insight: Every domino covers one black and one white square, but both removed corners are the same colour.
redHerring: Trying to construct a tiling or count them with a transfer matrix.
hints: Colour the board as a chessboard. What does each domino cover?
What colour are the two removed squares?
Count black and white squares that remain.
solution: Each domino covers one black and one white square, so any tiling covers equally many of each. Opposite corners share a colour, so the remaining board has 30 squares of one colour and 32 of the other. No tiling exists: the answer is $0$.
